**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Typical Value / Description |
|----------|----------|-----------------------------|
| **Basic Identity** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| **Physical State at STP** | Phase | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (120.2 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (14 K) |
| | Density (gas, 0 °C, 1 atm) | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume (ideal gas) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (Cp) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Heat of fusion | 0.000 kJ mol⁻¹ (negligible) |
| | Refractive index (visible) | 1.000132 |
| | Viscosity (at 20 °C) | 8.76 × 10⁻⁶ Pa·s |
| | Surface tension (at 20 °C) | 0.002 N m⁻¹ |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation state | +1 (in most compounds) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | 0.754 eV |
| | Standard enthalpy of formation (gas) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation (gas) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard entropy (gas) | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Standard molar volume (gas) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive as a reducing agent; forms H₂O, H₂S, hydrocarbons, etc. |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (ΔH° = –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (HF) or base (H₂O) depending on context. |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C (≈0.0006 M) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Very high in non‑polar solvents (e.g., methane, ethane). |
| **Spectroscopic Properties** | Rotational constant (H₂) | 59.3 cm⁻¹ |
| | Vibrational frequency (H₂) | 4401 cm⁻¹ |
| | Ionization potential (H atom) | 13.598 eV |
| | Lyman series limit | 91.2 nm |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Stable, most abundant (≈99.98 %) |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, 0.015 % natural abundance |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (half‑life 12.32 y), used in nuclear fusion and radiolabeling |
| **Applications & Significance** | Fuel cell fuel | Produces electricity via H₂ + O₂ → H₂O |
| | Rocket propellant | Liquid H₂ + liquid O₂ (high specific impulse) |
| | Metallurgy | Reducing agent for metal extraction |
| | Chemical synthesis | Hydrogenation, hydroformylation, etc. |
| | Nuclear fusion | D‑T fusion (tritium + deuterium) → He + neutron |
| | Scientific research | Standard for calibrating instruments, studying fundamental physics |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Only one proton and one electron (except for isotopes).
- **Highly reactive**: Forms a wide range of compounds; its diatomic form (H₂) is a powerful reducing agent.
- **Low boiling/melting points**: Remains gaseous under most Earth conditions.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium (stable), deuterium (stable), tritium (radioactive) each with distinct nuclear properties.
- **Energy carrier**: Central to clean‑energy technologies (fuel cells, hydrogen economy) and nuclear fusion research.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
